title: Uniform projective field-fibre regularity and vanishing
statement:
Fix $n\geq0$ and a numerical polynomial $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$ (integer-valued at all sufficiently large integers). There exists an integer $m\geq1$, depending only on $n,P$, such that for every algebraically closed field $k$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and every closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] whose coordinate Hilbert polynomial is $P$ [def-sfb-projective-coordinate-hilbert-polynomial], the ideal $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_k}\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent] and $m$-regular, meaning $H^j(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal J(m-j))=0$ for $1\leq j\leq n$. Here twists are as in [def-pc-projective-space-twist], $\mathcal O_Z(d)=i^*\mathcal O(d)$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and $H^j$ is module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]. For every integer $d\geq m$ and every $j>0$,
$$H^j(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal J(d))=H^j(Z,\mathcal O_Z(d))=0,$$
and the canonical restriction map fits into an exact sequence of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces
$$0\longrightarrow H^0(\mathbf P^n_k,\mathcal J(d))\longrightarrow k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_d\longrightarrow H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z(d))\longrightarrow0,$$
with $\dim_kH^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z(d))=P(d)$. This includes $n=0$ and $Z=\varnothing$.

proof.text: The item's $\mathbf P^n_k$ is $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};\operatorname{Spec}k)=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_n])$, while the cited lemmas are stated for $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$, $S=k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$. Apply the Proj scalar-extension lemma with $R=\mathbf Z$, $S=k$, $A=\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$ and the graded $k$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\to S$, $c\otimes T_a\mapsto cx_a$, of the polynomial scalar-extension lemma (it sends monomials to monomials of the same degree). Its cartesian square identifies $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};\operatorname{Spec}k)$; the preimage of $D_+(T_a)$ is $D_+(x_a)$ and on that chart the identification is $F/T_a^d\mapsto\beta(1\otimes F)/x_a^d$. Hence the standard charts, their dehomogenizations used in the coordinate-polynomial definition, and the twists $\mathcal O(d)$ glued from these charts agree on the two models; we transport $i$ along this isomorphism and work on $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ from now on. Put $X=\mathbf P^n_k$ and $\mathcal F=i_*\mathcal O_Z$. The field coordinate--Euler lemma makes $Z$ and $X$ (apply it also to the identity of $X$) proper Noetherian schemes with coherent structure sheaves. The chartwise homogeneous-ideal lemma identifies $Z$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(S/I)$ for the actual ideal $I=\bigoplus I_d(i)$ in the coordinate-polynomial definition: its chartwise kernels are already linear subspaces, so taking their linear spans changes nothing. Thus the coordinate--Euler lemma and the hypothesis give $P=Q_Z$ by uniqueness, and $\chi(Z,\mathcal O_Z(t))=P(t)$ for every integer $t$. The closed-immersion lemma gives coherence of $\mathcal F$, and the coherent-kernel lemma gives coherence of $\mathcal J$. The closed-immersion definition gives the surjection in $0\to\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal F\to0$.

Apply the closed-immersion projection and cohomology isomorphisms to obtain $H^q(X,\mathcal F(t))\cong H^q(Z,\mathcal O_Z(t))$ for all $q,t$. Hence the exact coherent quotient of step 1 has $\chi(X,\mathcal F(t))=P(t)$ for every integer $t$. The free-quotient kernel bound with $r=1$ supplies an integer $a$ depending only on $n,P$, for which $\mathcal J$ is $a$-regular. Set $m=\max(1,a)$. The upward-regularity clause makes $\mathcal J$ $m$-regular. This single $m$ works over every field, and therefore over every algebraically closed field in the item.

proof.text: For any integer $d$, tensor the sequence of step 1 by $\mathcal O_X(d)$. On each standard chart the twist is free with its specified basis, so this is the original exact sequence in that basis; exactness is local and is therefore preserved. The closed-immersion projection isomorphism identifies its last term with $i_*\mathcal O_Z(d)$. We have the specified short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal J(d)\to\mathcal O_X(d)\to i_*\mathcal O_Z(d)\to0$, whose last arrow is restriction: on a trivializing chart it is the quotient of functions defining the closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 01Y6 (lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent); projection formula for an invertible twist, locally the identity; constructions.tex Tag 03GL (lemma-closed-in-projective-space)

proof.text: Fix $d\geq m$. The regularity-consequences lemma gives $H^q(X,\mathcal J(d))=0$ for every $q>0$. Since $d\geq1$, the projective-space computation gives $H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ for $q>0$ and a $k$-linear isomorphism $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]_d$. That statement does not specify the map, so we check that the canonical map is one. Let $\sigma_d:S_d\to H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ send $F$ to the section equal to $(F/x_a^d)e_a^{(d)}$ on $U_a$; these agree on overlaps by the transition rule $e_a^{(d)}=(x_a/x_b)^de_b^{(d)}$ of the twist definition. It is injective: on $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}k[x_1/x_0,\ldots,x_n/x_0]$ the dehomogenization $F\mapsto F(1,x_1/x_0,\ldots,x_n/x_0)$ is injective on homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$, since distinct monomials of degree $d$ go to distinct monomials. Both sides have the same finite dimension by the projective-space computation, so $\sigma_d$ is an isomorphism; this is the monomial identification used below. Apply the closed-cokernel cohomology sequence to step 3. For $j>0$ its segment $H^j(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\to H^j(Z,\mathcal O_Z(d))\to H^{j+1}(X,\mathcal J(d))$ has zero outside terms, giving the required vanishing on $Z$. Its initial segment ends with $H^1(X,\mathcal J(d))=0$, giving exactly the asserted short exact restriction sequence. Under the monomial identification the middle arrow sends a homogeneous polynomial to its restricted section, because step 3 is the quotient map on every standard chart.

source.place: Tags 08A6 (lemma-m-regular-up), 01XT (lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring); curves.tex Tag 0BYD (lemma-genus-plane-curve), the same twisted-ideal long exact sequence

proof.text: The middle space of this exact sequence has its finite monomial basis, so its subspace $H^0(X,\mathcal J(d))$ and quotient $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z(d))$ are finite-dimensional. By the Euler-characteristic definition and the positive-degree vanishing just proved, $\dim_k H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z(d))=\chi(Z,\mathcal O_Z(d))=Q_Z(d)=P(d)$. No bound depending on $Z$ was introduced. For $n=0$, regularity has no conditions and the projective-space computation explicitly gives no positive cohomology. For $Z=\varnothing$, $\mathcal F=0$, $\mathcal J=\mathcal O_X$, and $Q_Z=P=0$; the sequence reduces to the monomial identification. If no fibre realizes $P$, the universal assertion is vacuous and the bound still exists by the free-quotient lemma.
